requirements.requirement: Restore the invoices listed in restore-request.txt into live/ and do not restore unrelated archived files.
requirements.summary: The request named INV-100.txt and INV-101.txt. Extraction reported only those members, and the resulting live tree contained those invoices plus the pre-existing customer register; archived old-notes.txt remained absent. The selective state persisted after restart.

requirements.requirement: Recover the requested invoices with their archived bytes and file modes.
requirements.summary: For both invoices, live SHA-256 hashes exactly matched hashes computed from the archive streams, and the live mode 0644 matched the archive listing. These checks passed both before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Retain the current contents of the newer live customer register.
requirements.summary: customers.csv retained its prepared 52-byte content and SHA-256 hash 0f060a93ce03b8a38e00181862fc775d127160011235f60f4d040afd98e84d51 before restoration, after restoration, and after restart; the older archived customer file was not restored.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 24.04 and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic were directly observed before and after the work. The executor used the platform's existing tar and standard system utilities, with no package or OS replacement recorded; package health remained good.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct and coherent evidence. The two requested invoices were selectively restored with matching bytes and modes, the newer customer register was preserved, unrelated archived content remained absent, and the installed OS and kernel were unchanged. The mandatory node restart and recovery protocol also passed completely.
limitations: Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

The selective tar extraction was the required task mutation (cmd-c4be6df8a2dd4f40), while the scheduled reboot was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol (cmd-66abef6f9bee4bdd). Other commands were read-only validation or bounded checks. The transient reboot units did not leave observed failed services or unsafe exposure; package health remained intact, and lifecycle differences were consistent with the reboot. The restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart system and data state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot ID, and recovered system and persistent data state were directly shown and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.
